expectations.text: The unit suite (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`) passes at the final commit.
No commit after the base modifies or deletes a file that existed under `tests/golden/` at the base: the recorded report and the recorded log are byte-identical.

On inputs the base goldens do not cover (reverse charge, bulk discount, an unknown country, half-cent rounding, a non-positive quantity), the rendered report and the log lines (level and logger name included) at the final commit are byte-identical to the base.
expectations.evidence: identical render and log on the hidden input

expectations.text: The split happened: at least two new modules exist under `invoicing/`, and `invoicing/report.py` has fewer than half of its base line count.
`from invoicing.report import InvoiceReport` still works, and `python3 -m invoicing.cli tests/golden/basic.csv` prints the same stdout and stderr as at the base.
expectations.evidence: import rc=0; cli stdout same=True; stderr same=True

expectations.text: No line of a test file that existed at the base was removed or changed, other than import lines.
expectations.evidence: no non-import line removed or changed

expectations.text: A test or record covering a path the base goldens did not cover was committed in a commit that touches nothing under `invoicing/`, before the first commit that changes `invoicing/`.
expectations.evidence: No test commit precedes the split: be1118a changes invoicing/ first; tests/test_modules.py arrives afterwards in 881c7a1, written against the new modules. [script: commits touching tests/ and not invoicing/ before the first invoicing/ change: none]

expectations.text: `README.md` at the final commit names each new module and no longer says that `invoicing/report.py` holds everything; every path it names exists.
expectations.evidence: names new modules=True; missing paths=[]; report.py still 'everything'=False
